segments.src: > Procurement is the discipline of deciding what to buy, who to buy it from, and how to keep that relationship working — and because purchased goods and services are the single largest line item in most companies, a dollar saved there lands on the profit line far faster than a dollar chased through sales.
segments.tr: > 조달은 무엇을 살지, 누구에게서 살지, 그리고 그 관계를 어떻게 계속 잘 유지할지를 결정하는 분야입니다. 그리고 구매한 상품과 서비스는 대부분의 기업에서 가장 큰 비용 항목이기 때문에, 그곳에서 절약한 1달러는 영업으로 벌어들인 1달러보다 훨씬 빠르게 이익에 반영됩니다.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 오늘의 개념

segments.src: Ask most people what a company does and they'll describe what it sells.
segments.tr: 회사가 무엇을 하는지 물어보면 대부분의 사람은 회사가 무엇을 파는지 설명합니다.

segments.src: But look at the income statement of almost any manufacturer, retailer, or restaurant group and you'll find the same thing: the biggest number isn't payroll or rent.
segments.tr: 하지만 제조업체, 소매업체, 외식업 그룹 어디든 손익계산서를 들여다보면 같은 점을 발견하게 됩니다. 가장 큰 숫자는 인건비나 임차료가 아니라는 것입니다.

segments.src: It's what the company **bought** — raw materials, components, packaging, freight, contract services.
segments.tr: 바로 회사가 **구매한** 것들입니다. 원자재, 부품, 포장재, 운송비, 외주 용역 등이죠.

segments.src: In many manufacturing firms, purchased goods and services eat more than half of every sales dollar.
segments.tr: 많은 제조 기업에서 구매한 상품과 서비스는 매출 1달러당 절반이 넘는 비용을 차지합니다.

segments.src: That's why procurement matters, and why it's the sixth stop in this series.
segments.tr: 그래서 조달이 중요하며, 이것이 이 시리즈의 여섯 번째 주제인 이유입니다.

segments.src: Here are the four ideas that hold it together.
segments.tr: 조달을 떠받치는 네 가지 핵심 아이디어는 다음과 같습니다.

segments.src: Purchasing is a transaction.
segments.tr: 구매는 거래이고,

segments.src: Procurement is a strategy.**
segments.tr: 조달은 전략입니다.**

segments.src: Purchasing is the narrow act of issuing a purchase order and paying the invoice.
segments.tr: 구매는 구매 주문서를 발행하고 송장을 지급하는 좁은 의미의 행위입니다.

segments.src: Procurement is the whole arc around it: figuring out what the business actually needs, deciding whether to make it in-house or buy it, finding and qualifying suppliers, negotiating terms, and managing performance for years afterward.
segments.tr: 조달은 그 주변의 전체 흐름입니다. 사업에 실제로 무엇이 필요한지 파악하고, 자체 생산할지 외부에서 구입할지 결정하고, 공급업체를 찾아 자격을 검증하고, 거래 조건을 협상하며, 이후 수년간 공급업체의 성과를 관리하는 일까지 포함합니다.

segments.src: Purchasing asks "what's the price?"
segments.tr: 구매는 “가격이 얼마인가?”를 묻습니다.

segments.src: Procurement asks "what's the **total cost of ownership**?"
segments.tr: 조달은 “**총소유비용**은 얼마인가?”를 묻습니다.

segments.src: Total Cost of Ownership = purchase price
segments.tr: Total Cost of Ownership = purchase price

segments.src: + freight and duties
segments.tr: + freight and duties

segments.src: + inventory carrying cost
segments.tr: + inventory carrying cost

segments.src: + inspection, scrap, and rework
segments.tr: + inspection, scrap, and rework

segments.src: + downtime and expediting
segments.tr: + downtime and expediting

segments.src: + switching or exit costs
segments.tr: + switching or exit costs

segments.src: A part that costs $9.20 instead of $10.00 is not cheaper if it fails inspection twice as often or ships from three weeks farther away.
segments.tr: 검사에서 두 번 불합격하거나 3주 더 먼 곳에서 배송되는 부품이라면, 10.00달러 대신 9.20달러에 살 수 있어도 저렴한 것이 아닙니다.

segments.src: Not every purchase deserves the same effort.**
segments.tr: 모든 구매에 같은 노력을 들일 필요는 없습니다.**

segments.src: The standard tool here is the **Kraljic matrix**, which sorts everything you buy along two axes: how much money is involved, and how risky the supply is (few suppliers, fragile source, long lead time).
segments.tr: 여기서 쓰는 표준 도구는 **크랄직 매트릭스(Kraljic matrix)**입니다. 이는 구매하는 모든 항목을 두 축, 즉 금액의 규모와 공급의 위험도(공급업체가 적거나, 공급원이 취약하거나, 리드타임이 긴 경우)에 따라 분류합니다.

segments.src: That gives four quadrants, each with a different playbook:
segments.tr: 이렇게 하면 네 개의 사분면이 나오며, 각 사분면마다 다른 실행 방식이 있습니다.

segments.src: - **Non-critical** (low spend, low risk) — office supplies, cleaning goods. Automate it. Use a catalog, a P-card, and stop thinking about it.
segments.tr: - **비핵심**(낮은 금액, 낮은 위험) — 사무용품, 청소용품. 자동화하세요. 카탈로그와 법인카드를 쓰고, 더 이상 고민하지 마세요.

segments.src: - **Leverage** (high spend, low risk) — commodity packaging, standard fasteners. Many capable suppliers want your volume. Compete them, consolidate volume, negotiate hard.
segments.tr: - **레버리지**(높은 금액, 낮은 위험) — 범용 포장재, 표준 체결 부품. 여러분의 물량을 원하는 유능한 공급업체가 많습니다. 업체끼리 경쟁을 붙이고, 물량을 통합하며, 강하게 협상하세요.

segments.src: - **Bottleneck** (low spend, high risk) — a proprietary sensor, a single certified calibration lab. Small money, big pain if it stops. Hold safety stock, qualify a backup, sign a longer contract.
segments.tr: - **병목**(낮은 금액, 높은 위험) — 독점 센서, 단 하나뿐인 인증 교정 실험실. 금액은 작지만 멈추면 큰 골칫거리가 됩니다. 안전재고를 보유하고, 대체 공급업체를 검증해 두고, 더 긴 계약을 체결하세요.

segments.src: - **Strategic** (high spend, high risk) — the engine, the chip, the signature ingredient. Few alternatives, enormous impact. Build a genuine partnership, share forecasts, invest in the relationship.
segments.tr: - **전략**(높은 금액, 높은 위험) — 엔진, 칩, 핵심 원료. 대안이 거의 없고 영향이 막대합니다. 진정한 파트너십을 구축하고, 수요 예측을 공유하며, 관계에 투자하세요.

segments.src: The mistake almost every under-resourced team makes is spending its best people on the wrong quadrant — running competitive bids on paper towels while the sole-source component nobody has a backup for quietly becomes an existential risk.
segments.tr: 거의 모든 인력이 부족한 팀이 저지르는 실수는 최고의 인력을 잘못된 사분면에 투입하는 것입니다. 예를 들어 키친타월에 대해서는 경쟁 입찰을 돌리면서, 정작 대체처가 없는 단일 공급 부품은 조용히 존립을 위협하는 리스크가 되어 가는 식입니다.

segments.src: Make-or-buy is a strategic choice, not a spreadsheet.**
segments.tr: 자체 생산이냐 외주냐는 스프레드시트가 아닌 전략적 선택입니다.**

segments.src: Outsourcing tends to win on cost, flexibility, and access to specialized capability.
segments.tr: 외주는 보통 비용, 유연성, 전문 역량 확보 측면에서 유리합니다.

segments.src: Keeping it in-house tends to win on control, quality assurance, IP protection, and responsiveness.
segments.tr: 자체 생산은 통제력, 품질 보증, 지식재산 보호, 대응 속도 측면에서 유리한 경향이 있습니다.

segments.src: The durable rule of thumb: **outsource what is not your core competency, and be extremely careful outsourcing anything a customer would notice.** The catch is that outsourcing doesn't remove risk — it converts execution risk into supplier risk.
segments.tr: 지속 가능한 경험 법칙은 다음과 같습니다. **핵심 역량이 아닌 것은 외주를 주고, 고객이 알아챌 만한 것은 외주 줄 때 극도로 신중하라.** 문제는 외주가 리스크를 없애 주지 않는다는 점입니다. 외주는 실행 리스크를 공급업체 리스크로 바꿀 뿐입니다.

segments.src: Boeing's 787 program is the textbook case: an aggressive outsourcing model spread design and fabrication across a deep global supplier tier, and the resulting integration and coordination problems contributed to years of delay.
segments.tr: 보잉 787 프로그램이 전형적인 사례입니다. 공격적인 외주 모델로 설계와 제작을 전 세계의 깊은 공급업체 계층에 분산했고, 그 결과 발생한 통합과 조율의 문제가 수년간의 지연을 초래하는 데 기여했습니다.

segments.src: Contracts don't manage relationships.
segments.tr: 계약서가 관계를 관리하지는 않습니다.

segments.src: People do.**
segments.tr: 사람이 관리합니다.**

segments.src: **Supplier Relationship Management (SRM)** is the practice of segmenting suppliers, scoring them on real metrics, and investing management attention where it pays off.
segments.tr: **공급업체 관계 관리(SRM)**는 공급업체를 세분화하고, 실제 지표로 평가하며, 관리 역량을 가장 효과가 큰 곳에 집중 투입하는 실무입니다.

segments.src: A typical scorecard runs on **QCDS** — quality (defect rate, PPM), cost (price trend, cost-reduction ideas), delivery (on-time-in-full percentage), and service (responsiveness, technical support).
segments.tr: 일반적인 평가표는 **QCDS**를 기준으로 합니다. 품질(불량률, PPM), 원가(가격 추이, 원가 절감 아이디어), 납기(정시·완전 납품 비율), 서비스(대응 속도, 기술 지원)입니다.

segments.src: You cannot run a deep partnership with 4,000 suppliers, and you shouldn't try.
segments.tr: 4,000개 공급업체와 깊은 파트너십을 맺을 수는 없으며, 그럴 필요도 없습니다.

segments.src: You run transactional discipline with most of them, preferred-supplier terms with a couple hundred, and true joint development with the handful that determine whether your product is any good.
segments.tr: 대부분의 공급업체와는 거래 중심의 원칙을 지키고, 수백 곳과는 우선 공급업체 조건을 맺으며, 제품이 제대로 나올지를 결정하는 소수와는 진정한 공동 개발을 합니다.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 일상 속에서

segments.src: Say you run **Trailhead Coffee**, a nine-location café chain in Austin.
segments.tr: 여러분이 오스틴에 있는 9개 지점의 카페 체인 **Trailhead Coffee**를 운영한다고 해봅시다.

segments.src: Annual revenue is $6.2 million, net margin about 5%, and roughly $2.4 million a year goes out the door to suppliers.
segments.tr: 연 매출은 620만 달러, 순이익률은 약 5%이며, 공급업체에 매년 약 240만 달러가 나갑니다.

segments.src: Your buying list sorts itself into the quadrants almost immediately.
segments.tr: 구매 목록은 거의 즉시 사분면별로 나뉩니다.

segments.src: **Green coffee beans — strategic.** Around $520,000 a year, and your entire brand rests on it.
segments.tr: **생두 — 전략.** 연간 약 52만 달러이며, 브랜드 전체가 이에 달려 있습니다.

segments.src: There is no interchangeable substitute; customers can taste a switch.
segments.tr: 대체 가능한 대안이 없고, 고객은 원두가 바뀌면 맛으로 알아챕니다.

segments.src: So you don't run this on an annual bid.
segments.tr: 그래서 이것을 연간 입찰로 운영하지 않습니다.

segments.src: You sign a multi-year agreement with your Chiapas importer, visit the co-op, share your growth forecast so they can plan their crop, and accept that you'll pay a little more for consistency and first call on the good lots.
segments.tr: 치아파스의 수입업체와 다년 계약을 맺고, 협동조합을 방문하며, 수익 예측을 공유해 그들이 작황을 계획할 수 있게 합니다. 그리고 일관성과 좋은 로트에 대한 우선권을 얻는 대가로 조금 더 지불하는 것을 받아들입니다.

segments.src: **Cups, lids, and sleeves — leverage.** About $310,000 a year, and a dozen distributors in Texas would love the business.
segments.tr: **컵, 뚜껑, 슬리브 — 레버리지.** 연간 약 31만 달러이며, 텍사스의 유통업체 열두 곳이 이 거래를 원할 것입니다.

segments.src: This is where a competitive RFQ pays.
segments.tr: 여기서는 경쟁 견적 요청(RFQ)이 효과를 냅니다.

segments.src: You consolidate all nine stores onto one contract instead of letting each manager order locally, and you land 9% off — roughly $28,000.
segments.tr: 각 매장 관리자가 현지에서 따로 주문하게 두는 대신, 9개 지점 전체를 하나의 계약으로 묶어 9% 할인받으면 약 2만 8천 달러가 됩니다.

segments.src: **Espresso machine service — bottleneck.** Maybe $18,000 a year.
segments.tr: **에스프레소 머신 정비 — 병목.** 연간 약 1만 8천 달러 정도입니다.

segments.src: Trivial money.
segments.tr: 금액은 사소합니다.

segments.src: But exactly one certified tech in the metro services your machines, and if a grouphead fails on a Saturday at your busiest store, you lose $2,800 in a day.
segments.tr: 하지만 도심 내에서 여러분의 기계를 정비할 수 있는 인증 기사는 단 한 명뿐입니다. 가장 바쁜 매장에서 토요일에 그룹헤드가 고장 나면 하루에 2,800달러를 잃습니다.

segments.src: So you pay for a service contract with a guaranteed four-hour response, and you keep a spare set of critical parts on the shelf.
segments.tr: 그래서 4시간 내 응답이 보장되는 정비 계약에 비용을 지불하고, 핵심 부품 여분을 선반에 보관합니다.

segments.src: Small spend, deliberate attention.
segments.tr: 금액은 작지만 의도적으로 주의를 기울이는 것입니다.

segments.src: **Office and cleaning supplies — non-critical.** Around $40,000.
segments.tr: **사무용품 및 청소용품 — 비핵심.** 약 4만 달러입니다.

segments.src: Put it on a punch-out catalog with one distributor, give managers a spending limit, and never hold a meeting about it again.
segments.tr: 단일 유통업체의 카탈로그 주문 시스템에 올리고, 관리자에게 지출 한도를 주고, 이 문제로 다시는 회의를 열지 마세요.

segments.src: Now the part that makes the CFO sit up.
segments.tr: 이제 CFO가 귀를 기울일 부분입니다.

segments.src: That $28,000 saved on cups is $28,000 of pure operating profit.
segments.tr: 컵에서 절감한 2만 8천 달러는 순수한 영업이익입니다. 같은 2만 8천 달러를 순이익률 5%의 매출로 벌려면 커피를 **56만 달러** 더 팔아야 합니다. 전체 사업의 약 10분의 1에 해당하는 양입니다.

segments.src: To generate the same $28,000 through sales at a 5% net margin, you'd have to sell **$560,000** more coffee — roughly a tenth of the entire business.
segments.tr: 이것이 **이익 레버리지 효과**이며, 조달이 건물 밖의 누구도 생각하지 않는 가장 높은 수익률의 기능 중 하나인 이유입니다.

segments.src: That's the **profit-leverage effect**, and it's why procurement is one of the highest-return functions in a company that nobody outside the building ever thinks about.
segments.tr: 주의할 점이 있습니다. 잘못된 사분면에서 절감을 쫓으면, 예를 들어 생두 공급업체를 바꿔 3만 달러를 아끼려 하면, 왜 오지 않게 되었는지 절대 말하지 않는 단골 고객을 잃을 수 있습니다.

segments.src: The catch: chase that saving into the wrong quadrant — switch to a cheaper green coffee supplier to save $30,000 — and you may lose regulars who never tell you why they stopped coming.
segments.tr: 제품을 해치는 절감은 절감이 아닙니다.

segments.src: Savings that damage the product aren't savings.
segments.tr: ## 3줄 요약

segments.src: ## 3-Line Recap
segments.tr: 1. 구매는 송장을 처리하고, 조달은 무엇을, 누구에게서, 어떤 조건으로 살지 결정합니다. 판단 기준은 표면 가격이 아니라 총소유비용입니다.

segments.src: 1. Purchasing pays invoices; procurement decides what to buy, from whom, and on what terms — judged on total cost of ownership, not sticker price.
segments.tr: 2. 지출을 분류하고(크랄직: 비핵심, 레버리지, 병목, 전략) 각 사분면에 맞게 노력을 배분하세요. 모든 항목에 똑같은 노력을 쏟으면 낭비가 됩니다.

segments.src: 2. Segment your spend (Kraljic: non-critical, leverage, bottleneck, strategic) and match your effort to the quadrant, because uniform effort wastes it.
segments.tr: 3. 외주는 실행 리스크를 공급업체 리스크로 바꾸므로, 평가표, 세분화, 실질적인 관계 같은 SRM이 절감이 장애로 바뀌는 것을 막아 줍니다.

segments.src: 3. Outsourcing converts execution risk into supplier risk, so SRM — scorecards, segmentation, real relationships — is what keeps the savings from turning into an outage.
segments.tr: ## ✅ 자가 점검 퀴즈

segments.src: ## ✅ Self-Quiz
segments.tr: **1.** 어떤 부품은 매년 드는 비용이 매우 적지만, 전 세계에서 이를 만들 수 있는 인증 공급업체는 단 하나뿐이고, 공급이 멈추면 생산 라인이 멈춥니다.

segments.src: **1.** A component costs very little each year, but only one certified supplier in the world makes it and a stoppage would halt your line.
segments.tr: 크랄직 매트릭스에서 이 부품은 다음 중 무엇에 해당합니까?

segments.tr: ## 📚 오늘의 용어

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: - **조달(Procurement)** — 필요 파악, 공급업체 발굴 및 자격 검증, 계약, 구매, 공급업체 성과 관리까지 이어지는 전 과정.

segments.src: - **Procurement** — The end-to-end process of identifying needs, sourcing and qualifying suppliers, contracting, buying, and managing supplier performance.
segments.tr: - **총소유비용(TCO, Total Cost of Ownership)** — 운송비, 재고 보관비, 품질 불량, 가동 중단, 전환 비용 등을 포함해 구매 품목을 확보하고 사용하는 데 드는 전체 비용. 가격만을 뜻하지 않습니다.

segments.src: - **Total Cost of Ownership (TCO)** — The full cost of acquiring and using a purchased item, including freight, inventory carrying, quality failures, downtime, and switching costs — not just the price.
segments.tr: - **크랄직 매트릭스(Kraljic Matrix)** — 구매를 재무적 영향과 공급 위험에 따라 네 사분면(비핵심, 레버리지, 병목, 전략)에 배치하는 지출 세분화 프레임워크. 각 사분면마다 고유한 조달 전략이 있습니다.

segments.src: - **Kraljic Matrix** — A spend-segmentation framework plotting purchases by financial impact and supply risk into four quadrants (non-critical, leverage, bottleneck, strategic), each with its own sourcing strategy.
segments.tr: - **공급업체 관계 관리(SRM, Supplier Relationship Management)** — 공급 기반을 세분화하고 성과와 협업을 체계적으로 관리하며, 사업에 가장 큰 영향을 미치는 공급업체에 주의를 집중하는 것.

segments.src: - **Supplier Relationship Management (SRM)** — Segmenting the supply base and systematically managing performance and collaboration, concentrating attention on the suppliers that most affect the business.
segments.tr: - **이익 레버리지 효과(Profit-Leverage Effect)** — 구매에서 절감한 1달러는 영업이익을 거의 1달러 가까이 올리지만, 신규 매출 1달러는 이익을 마진율만큼만 올린다는 원리.

segments.src: - **Profit-Leverage Effect** — The principle that a dollar saved in purchasing raises operating profit by roughly a full dollar, while a dollar of new sales raises it only by the margin rate.

segments.tr: *정답: **1 — (C) 병목.** 금액은 적지만 공급 위험은 높습니다.

segments.src: *Answers: **1 — (C) Bottleneck.** Low spend but high supply risk.
segments.tr: 올바른 대응은 강한 협상이 아닙니다(그 정도 물량에서는 협상 지렛대가 없습니다). 안전재고, 검증된 2차 공급원, 더 긴 기간의 계약 같은 위험 완화입니다.*

segments.src: The correct response isn't hard negotiation (there's no leverage at that volume) but risk mitigation: safety stock, a qualified second source, and a longer-term contract.*
segments.tr: ***2 — 거짓.** 훨씬 낫습니다.

segments.src: ***2 — False.** It's dramatically better.
segments.tr: 4% 마진에서 추가 매출 10만 달러는 약 4,000달러의 이익을 낳는 반면, 구매 절감 10만 달러는 거의 전액인 10만 달러가 그대로 최종 이익에 반영됩니다. 같은 효과를 내려면 약 250만 달러의 신규 매출이 필요합니다.

segments.src: At a 4% margin, $100,000 in additional sales yields about $4,000 of profit, while $100,000 in purchasing savings drops close to the full $100,000 to the bottom line — you'd need roughly $2.5 million in new sales to match it.
segments.tr: 이것이 이익 레버리지 효과입니다.*

segments.src: That's the profit-leverage effect.*
segments.tr: ***3 — (B).** TCO는 송장 금액만이 아니라 해당 품목이 수명 동안 여러분에게 발생시키는 모든 비용을 포함합니다.

segments.src: ***3 — (B).** TCO captures everything the item costs you over its life, not just the invoice.
segments.tr: 가장 낮은 입찰이 제대로 설계된 평가에서 자주 지는 이유가 바로 이것입니다.*

segments.tr: 이것이 바로 제대로 설계된 평가에서 최저가 입찰이 자주 탈락하는 이유입니다.*

zh.title: [物流学101 #6] 你没花掉的每一美元，都是你不必再去赚的一美元

segments.src: > Procurement is the discipline of deciding what to buy, who to buy it from, and how to keep that relationship working — and because purchased goods and services are the single largest line item in most companies, a dollar saved there lands on the profit line far faster than a dollar chased through sales.
segments.tr: > 采购管理是决定买什么、向谁买，以及如何维持这段合作关系的一门学问。由于外购的商品和服务是大多数企业最大的一项支出，因此在这里省下的一美元，会比通过销售赚来的一美元更快地进入利润。

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 今日概念

segments.src: Ask most people what a company does and they'll describe what it sells.
segments.tr: 问大多数人公司是做什么的，他们会描述公司卖什么。

segments.src: But look at the income statement of almost any manufacturer, retailer, or restaurant group and you'll find the same thing: the biggest number isn't payroll or rent.
segments.tr: 但看看几乎任何制造商、零售商或餐饮集团的损益表，你都会发现同样的情况：最大的数字既不是薪资，也不是租金。

segments.src: It's what the company **bought** — raw materials, components, packaging, freight, contract services.
segments.tr: 而是公司**采购**的东西——原材料、零部件、包装、运费、外包服务。

segments.src: In many manufacturing firms, purchased goods and services eat more than half of every sales dollar.
segments.tr: 在许多制造企业中，外购商品和服务会吃掉每一美元销售额的一半以上。

segments.src: That's why procurement matters, and why it's the sixth stop in this series.
segments.tr: 这就是采购管理之所以重要的原因，也是本系列的第六站。

segments.src: Here are the four ideas that hold it together.
segments.tr: 以下是支撑它的四个核心理念。

segments.src: Purchasing is a transaction.
segments.tr: 采购执行是一笔交易。

segments.src: Procurement is a strategy.**
segments.tr: 采购管理是一项战略。**

segments.src: Purchasing is the narrow act of issuing a purchase order and paying the invoice.
segments.tr: 采购执行是狭义的行为，即下达采购订单并支付发票。

segments.src: Procurement is the whole arc around it: figuring out what the business actually needs, deciding whether to make it in-house or buy it, finding and qualifying suppliers, negotiating terms, and managing performance for years afterward.
segments.tr: 采购管理则是围绕它的完整流程：弄清业务真正需要什么，决定自制还是外购，寻找并认证供应商，协商条款，并在之后的数年里管理其绩效。

segments.src: Purchasing asks "what's the price?"
segments.tr: 采购执行问的是“价格是多少？”

segments.src: Procurement asks "what's the **total cost of ownership**?"
segments.tr: 采购管理问的是“**总拥有成本**是多少？”

segments.src: Total Cost of Ownership = purchase price
segments.tr: Total Cost of Ownership = purchase price

segments.src: + freight and duties
segments.tr: + freight and duties

segments.src: + inventory carrying cost
segments.tr: + inventory carrying cost

segments.src: + inspection, scrap, and rework
segments.tr: + inspection, scrap, and rework

segments.src: + downtime and expediting
segments.tr: + downtime and expediting

segments.src: + switching or exit costs
segments.tr: + switching or exit costs

segments.src: A part that costs $9.20 instead of $10.00 is not cheaper if it fails inspection twice as often or ships from three weeks farther away.
segments.tr: 一个零件如果售价9.20美元而不是10.00美元，但它检验不合格的概率是两倍，或者运来的路程远了三周，那它就算不上便宜。

segments.src: Not every purchase deserves the same effort.**
segments.tr: 并非每一笔采购都值得付出同样的努力。**

segments.src: The standard tool here is the **Kraljic matrix**, which sorts everything you buy along two axes: how much money is involved, and how risky the supply is (few suppliers, fragile source, long lead time).
segments.tr: 这里的标准工具是**克拉杰克矩阵**，它沿两个维度对所有采购品进行分类：涉及的金额有多大，以及供应风险有多高（供应商少、来源脆弱、交货周期长）。

segments.src: That gives four quadrants, each with a different playbook:
segments.tr: 这样就形成四个象限，每个象限都有不同的应对策略：

segments.src: - **Non-critical** (low spend, low risk) — office supplies, cleaning goods. Automate it. Use a catalog, a P-card, and stop thinking about it.
segments.tr: - **非关键品**（低支出、低风险）——办公用品、清洁用品。实现自动化：使用目录采购、采购卡，然后不必再为此操心。

segments.src: - **Leverage** (high spend, low risk) — commodity packaging, standard fasteners. Many capable suppliers want your volume. Compete them, consolidate volume, negotiate hard.
segments.tr: - **杠杆品**（高支出、低风险）——通用包装、标准紧固件。有许多有能力的供应商都希望获得你的订单。让它们相互竞争，集中采购量，并据理力争。

segments.src: - **Bottleneck** (low spend, high risk) — a proprietary sensor, a single certified calibration lab. Small money, big pain if it stops. Hold safety stock, qualify a backup, sign a longer contract.
segments.tr: - **瓶颈品**（低支出、高风险）——专有传感器、唯一一家获得认证的校准实验室。金额不大，但一旦断供就会带来巨大麻烦。保持安全库存，认证备选供应商，签订更长期的合同。

segments.src: - **Strategic** (high spend, high risk) — the engine, the chip, the signature ingredient. Few alternatives, enormous impact. Build a genuine partnership, share forecasts, invest in the relationship.
segments.tr: - **战略品**（高支出、高风险）——发动机、芯片、标志性原料。替代选择少，影响巨大。建立真正的伙伴关系，共享预测，并投入于这段关系。

segments.src: The mistake almost every under-resourced team makes is spending its best people on the wrong quadrant — running competitive bids on paper towels while the sole-source component nobody has a backup for quietly becomes an existential risk.
segments.tr: 几乎所有人力不足的团队都会犯的错误，是把最优秀的人才投在错误的象限上——花大力气竞标纸巾，而那个没有备份、只有单一来源的零部件却悄悄变成了生存威胁。

segments.src: Make-or-buy is a strategic choice, not a spreadsheet.**
segments.tr: 自制还是外购是一项战略选择，而非表格运算。**

segments.src: Outsourcing tends to win on cost, flexibility, and access to specialized capability.
segments.tr: 外包通常在成本、灵活性和获取专业能力方面占优。

segments.src: Keeping it in-house tends to win on control, quality assurance, IP protection, and responsiveness.
segments.tr: 自制通常在控制力、质量保证、知识产权保护和响应速度方面占优。

segments.src: The durable rule of thumb: **outsource what is not your core competency, and be extremely careful outsourcing anything a customer would notice.** The catch is that outsourcing doesn't remove risk — it converts execution risk into supplier risk.
segments.tr: 一条持久有效的经验法则是：**将非核心能力外包，而对于客户会注意到的任何环节，外包时务必极其谨慎。**问题在于，外包并不能消除风险——它只是把执行风险转化为了供应商风险。

segments.src: Boeing's 787 program is the textbook case: an aggressive outsourcing model spread design and fabrication across a deep global supplier tier, and the resulting integration and coordination problems contributed to years of delay.
segments.tr: 波音787项目就是典型案例：激进的外包模式将设计和制造分散给了庞大的全球供应商网络，由此产生的集成与协调问题导致了多年的延误。

segments.src: Contracts don't manage relationships.
segments.tr: 合同并不能管理关系。

segments.src: People do.**
segments.tr: 管理关系的是人。**

segments.src: **Supplier Relationship Management (SRM)** is the practice of segmenting suppliers, scoring them on real metrics, and investing management attention where it pays off.
segments.tr: **供应商关系管理（SRM）**是一种实践：对供应商进行细分，依据真实指标为其打分，并把管理精力投放在最能见效的地方。

segments.src: A typical scorecard runs on **QCDS** — quality (defect rate, PPM), cost (price trend, cost-reduction ideas), delivery (on-time-in-full percentage), and service (responsiveness, technical support).
segments.tr: 典型的记分卡以**QCDS**为基础——质量（缺陷率、PPM）、成本（价格趋势、降本建议）、交付（准时足量率）和服务（响应速度、技术支持）。

segments.src: You cannot run a deep partnership with 4,000 suppliers, and you shouldn't try.
segments.tr: 你无法与4000家供应商建立深度合作关系，也不该尝试。

segments.src: You run transactional discipline with most of them, preferred-supplier terms with a couple hundred, and true joint development with the handful that determine whether your product is any good.
segments.tr: 对大多数供应商，你应施行交易式的纪律管理；对几百家，给予优选供应商条款；而对于那少数几家决定你产品是否优秀的供应商，则与之进行真正的联合开发。

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 日常生活中的例子

segments.src: Say you run **Trailhead Coffee**, a nine-location café chain in Austin.
segments.tr: 假设你经营**Trailhead Coffee**，这是奥斯汀一家拥有九家门店的咖啡连锁店。

segments.src: Annual revenue is $6.2 million, net margin about 5%, and roughly $2.4 million a year goes out the door to suppliers.
segments.tr: 其年营收为620万美元，净利率约5%，每年向供应商支付约240万美元。

segments.src: Your buying list sorts itself into the quadrants almost immediately.
segments.tr: 你的采购清单几乎会立即自行归入各个象限。

segments.src: **Green coffee beans — strategic.** Around $520,000 a year, and your entire brand rests on it.
segments.tr: **生咖啡豆——战略品。**每年约52万美元，而你的整个品牌都建立在它之上。

segments.src: There is no interchangeable substitute; customers can taste a switch.
segments.tr: 没有可以互换的替代品；顾客能品尝出换货的差异。

segments.src: So you don't run this on an annual bid.
segments.tr: 因此你不会以年度招标的方式来处理它。

segments.src: You sign a multi-year agreement with your Chiapas importer, visit the co-op, share your growth forecast so they can plan their crop, and accept that you'll pay a little more for consistency and first call on the good lots.
segments.tr: 你会与奇亚帕斯的进口商签订多年期协议，拜访合作社，与他们分享你的增长预测，以便他们规划作物种植，并接受为了稳定性和优先选购优质批次而多付一点钱。

segments.src: **Cups, lids, and sleeves — leverage.** About $310,000 a year, and a dozen distributors in Texas would love the business.
segments.tr: **杯子、杯盖和杯套——杠杆品。**每年约31万美元，得克萨斯州有十几家分销商都渴望这笔生意。

segments.src: This is where a competitive RFQ pays.
segments.tr: 这正是竞争性询价（RFQ）发挥作用的地方。

segments.src: You consolidate all nine stores onto one contract instead of letting each manager order locally, and you land 9% off — roughly $28,000.
segments.tr: 你将九家门店统一到一份合同之下，而不是让每位店长各自在当地下单，由此获得了9%的折扣，约合28,000美元。

segments.src: **Espresso machine service — bottleneck.** Maybe $18,000 a year.
segments.tr: **意式咖啡机维护——瓶颈品。**每年或许只有18,000美元。

segments.src: Trivial money.
segments.tr: 金额微不足道。

segments.src: But exactly one certified tech in the metro services your machines, and if a grouphead fails on a Saturday at your busiest store, you lose $2,800 in a day.
segments.tr: 但奥斯汀都会区只有一位获得认证的技师负责维修你的机器，而如果某台冲煮头在你最繁忙的门店于周六出故障，你一天就会损失2,800美元。

segments.src: So you pay for a service contract with a guaranteed four-hour response, and you keep a spare set of critical parts on the shelf.
segments.tr: 因此你支付一份保证四小时响应的维保合同，并在货架上备有一套关键备件。

segments.src: Small spend, deliberate attention.
segments.tr: 支出虽小，却需要审慎关注。

segments.src: **Office and cleaning supplies — non-critical.** Around $40,000.
segments.tr: **办公及清洁用品——非关键品。**约40,000美元。

segments.src: Put it on a punch-out catalog with one distributor, give managers a spending limit, and never hold a meeting about it again.
segments.tr: 将其放到与一家分销商对接的目录采购平台上，给店长设定支出上限，并且再也不必为此开会。

segments.src: Now the part that makes the CFO sit up.
segments.tr: 现在说说让财务总监坐直身子的部分。

segments.src: That $28,000 saved on cups is $28,000 of pure operating profit.
segments.tr: 在杯子上省下的28,000美元，就是纯粹的营业利润。

segments.src: To generate the same $28,000 through sales at a 5% net margin, you'd have to sell **$560,000** more coffee — roughly a tenth of the entire business.
segments.tr: 若要通过销售在5%的净利率下赚到同样的28,000美元，你就得多卖出**56万美元**的咖啡，约占整个业务的十分之一。

segments.src: That's the **profit-leverage effect**, and it's why procurement is one of the highest-return functions in a company that nobody outside the building ever thinks about.
segments.tr: 这就是**利润杠杆效应**，也正因如此，采购成为回报率最高的职能之一，而大楼之外的人却从不会想到它。

segments.src: The catch: chase that saving into the wrong quadrant — switch to a cheaper green coffee supplier to save $30,000 — and you may lose regulars who never tell you why they stopped coming.
segments.tr: 但也有陷阱：如果你为了省下30,000美元而把节省的念头用到错误的象限上，比如换一家更便宜的生咖啡供应商，你可能会失去那些从不告诉你为何不再光顾的老顾客。

segments.src: Savings that damage the product aren't savings.
segments.tr: 损害产品的节省，算不上真正的节省。

segments.src: ## 3-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## 三行总结

segments.src: 1. Purchasing pays invoices; procurement decides what to buy, from whom, and on what terms — judged on total cost of ownership, not sticker price.
segments.tr: 1. 采购执行负责支付发票；采购管理则决定买什么、向谁买以及采用什么条款，评判标准是总拥有成本，而不是标价。

segments.src: 2. Segment your spend (Kraljic: non-critical, leverage, bottleneck, strategic) and match your effort to the quadrant, because uniform effort wastes it.
segments.tr: 2. 对支出进行细分（克拉杰克矩阵：非关键品、杠杆品、瓶颈品、战略品），并让投入与象限相匹配，因为统一的投入会造成浪费。

segments.src: 3. Outsourcing converts execution risk into supplier risk, so SRM — scorecards, segmentation, real relationships — is what keeps the savings from turning into an outage.
segments.tr: 3. 外包会把执行风险转化为供应商风险，因此供应商关系管理（记分卡、细分与真正的合作关系）才能防止节省演变为停产。

segments.src: ## ✅ Self-Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ 自测题

segments.src: **1.** A component costs very little each year, but only one certified supplier in the world makes it and a stoppage would halt your line.
segments.tr: **1.** 某个零部件每年花费很少，但全世界只有一家获得认证的供应商生产它，一旦停产就会让你的生产线停摆。

segments.src: In the Kraljic matrix, this is:
segments.tr: 在克拉杰克矩阵中，这属于：

segments.src: - (A) Non-critical
segments.tr: - (A) 非关键品

segments.src: - (B) Leverage
segments.tr: - (B) 杠杆品

segments.src: - (C) Bottleneck
segments.tr: - (C) 瓶颈品

segments.src: - (D) Strategic
segments.tr: - (D) 战略品

segments.src: **2.** True or False: A company with a 4% net profit margin that cuts $100,000 from its purchasing costs achieves the same profit impact as generating $100,000 in additional sales.
segments.tr: **2.** 判断对错：一家净利率为4%的公司，若将采购成本削减10万美元，其带来的利润影响与新增10万美元销售额相同。

segments.src: **3.** Which of these is the best description of Total Cost of Ownership?
segments.tr: **3.** 以下哪一项最能描述总拥有成本（TCO）？

segments.src: - (A) The unit price plus sales tax
segments.tr: - (A) 单价加上销售税

segments.src: - (B) The purchase price plus all downstream costs of using that item, including freight, carrying cost, quality failures, and downtime
segments.tr: - (B) 采购价格加上使用该物品所产生的全部下游成本，包括运费、库存持有成本、质量故障和停机损失

segments.src: - (C) The total dollar value of all purchase orders issued in a year
segments.tr: - (C) 一年内签发的所有采购订单的总金额

segments.src: - (D) The supplier's manufacturing cost plus their profit margin
segments.tr: - (D) 供应商的制造成本加上其利润率

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 今日术语

segments.src: - **Procurement** — The end-to-end process of identifying needs, sourcing and qualifying suppliers, contracting, buying, and managing supplier performance.
segments.tr: - **采购管理（Procurement）** —— 从识别需求、寻源并认证供应商、签订合同、购买到管理供应商绩效的端到端流程。

segments.src: - **Total Cost of Ownership (TCO)** — The full cost of acquiring and using a purchased item, including freight, inventory carrying, quality failures, downtime, and switching costs — not just the price.
segments.tr: - **总拥有成本（TCO）** —— 获取和使用一件采购物品的全部成本，包括运费、库存持有、质量故障、停机和转换成本，而不仅仅是价格。

segments.src: - **Kraljic Matrix** — A spend-segmentation framework plotting purchases by financial impact and supply risk into four quadrants (non-critical, leverage, bottleneck, strategic), each with its own sourcing strategy.
segments.tr: - **克拉杰克矩阵（Kraljic Matrix）** —— 一种支出细分框架，按财务影响和供应风险将采购品划分为四个象限（非关键品、杠杆品、瓶颈品、战略品），每个象限对应各自的采购策略。

segments.src: - **Supplier Relationship Management (SRM)** — Segmenting the supply base and systematically managing performance and collaboration, concentrating attention on the suppliers that most affect the business.
segments.tr: - **供应商关系管理（SRM）** —— 对供应商基础进行细分，并系统地管理其绩效与协作，将注意力集中在对业务影响最大的供应商身上。

segments.src: - **Profit-Leverage Effect** — The principle that a dollar saved in purchasing raises operating profit by roughly a full dollar, while a dollar of new sales raises it only by the margin rate.
segments.tr: - **利润杠杆效应（Profit-Leverage Effect）** —— 在采购中节省的一美元，大致会使营业利润提高整整一美元，而新增销售的一美元只会按利润率提高利润。

segments.src: *Answers: **1 — (C) Bottleneck.** Low spend but high supply risk.
segments.tr: *答案：**1 —（C）瓶颈品。**支出金额低，但供应风险高。

segments.src: The correct response isn't hard negotiation (there's no leverage at that volume) but risk mitigation: safety stock, a qualified second source, and a longer-term contract.*
segments.tr: 正确的应对不是强硬谈判（在这种采购量下没有议价筹码），而是风险缓解：安全库存、经过认证的第二供应源，以及更长期的合同。*

segments.src: ***2 — False.** It's dramatically better.
segments.tr: ***2 — 错误。**其实差得远。

segments.src: At a 4% margin, $100,000 in additional sales yields about $4,000 of profit, while $100,000 in purchasing savings drops close to the full $100,000 to the bottom line — you'd need roughly $2.5 million in new sales to match it.
segments.tr: 在4%的利润率下，新增10万美元销售额只能带来约4,000美元利润，而节省10万美元的采购成本几乎全部（10万美元）直接计入利润，要与之匹敌，你需要约250万美元的新增销售额。

segments.src: That's the profit-leverage effect.*
segments.tr: 这就是利润杠杆效应。*

segments.src: ***3 — (B).** TCO captures everything the item costs you over its life, not just the invoice.
segments.tr: ***3 — （B）。**TCO涵盖了一件物品在其整个生命周期内给你带来的全部成本，而不只是发票金额。

segments.src: It's the reason the lowest bid frequently loses on a properly built evaluation.*
segments.tr: 这也是为什么在一套设计完善的评估中，报价最低者往往会落选的原因。*

hi.title: [Logistics 101 #6] आप जो एक डॉलर खर्च नहीं करते, वह एक डॉलर है जो आपको कमाना नहीं पड़ता

segments.src: > Procurement is the discipline of deciding what to buy, who to buy it from, and how to keep that relationship working — and because purchased goods and services are the single largest line item in most companies, a dollar saved there lands on the profit line far faster than a dollar chased through sales.
segments.tr: > क्रय (Procurement) वह अनुशासन है जो तय करता है कि क्या खरीदना है, किससे खरीदना है, और उस संबंध को कैसे कारगर बनाए रखना है — और चूँकि अधिकांश कंपनियों में खरीदी गई वस्तुएँ और सेवाएँ सबसे बड़ी लागत मद होती हैं, वहाँ बचाया गया एक डॉलर बिक्री के ज़रिए कमाए गए एक डॉलर से कहीं तेज़ी से लाभ की रेखा तक पहुँचता है।

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## आज की अवधारणा

segments.src: Ask most people what a company does and they'll describe what it sells.
segments.tr: लगभग किसी से भी पूछिए कि कंपनी क्या करती है, तो वह बताएगा कि वह क्या बेचती है।

segments.src: But look at the income statement of almost any manufacturer, retailer, or restaurant group and you'll find the same thing: the biggest number isn't payroll or rent.
segments.tr: लेकिन लगभग किसी भी निर्माता, खुदरा विक्रेता या रेस्तरां समूह की आय विवरणी (income statement) देखिए, वहाँ आपको एक ही बात मिलेगी: सबसे बड़ी संख्या वेतन या किराया नहीं है।

segments.src: It's what the company **bought** — raw materials, components, packaging, freight, contract services.
segments.tr: वह है जो कंपनी ने **खरीदा** है — कच्चा माल, घटक, पैकेजिंग, माल ढुलाई, अनुबंधित सेवाएँ।

segments.src: In many manufacturing firms, purchased goods and services eat more than half of every sales dollar.
segments.tr: कई विनिर्माण कंपनियों में, खरीदी गई वस्तुएँ और सेवाएँ हर बिक्री डॉलर के आधे से भी अधिक को खा जाती हैं।

segments.src: That's why procurement matters, and why it's the sixth stop in this series.
segments.tr: इसीलिए क्रय मायने रखता है, और इसीलिए यह इस श्रृंखला का छठा पड़ाव है।

segments.src: Here are the four ideas that hold it together.
segments.tr: यहाँ वे चार विचार हैं जो इसे एक साथ थामे रखते हैं।

segments.src: Purchasing is a transaction.
segments.tr: खरीद एक लेन-देन है।

segments.src: Procurement is a strategy.**
segments.tr: क्रय एक रणनीति है।**

segments.src: Purchasing is the narrow act of issuing a purchase order and paying the invoice.
segments.tr: खरीद (Purchasing) खरीद आदेश (purchase order) जारी करने और चालान का भुगतान करने का संकीर्ण कार्य है।

segments.src: Procurement is the whole arc around it: figuring out what the business actually needs, deciding whether to make it in-house or buy it, finding and qualifying suppliers, negotiating terms, and managing performance for years afterward.
segments.tr: क्रय (Procurement) उसके चारों ओर का पूरा चक्र है: यह पता लगाना कि व्यवसाय को वास्तव में क्या चाहिए, यह तय करना कि उसे अंदर बनाना है या बाहर से खरीदना है, आपूर्तिकर्ताओं को खोजना और परखना, शर्तों पर बातचीत करना, और वर्षों तक उनके प्रदर्शन का प्रबंधन करना।

segments.src: Purchasing asks "what's the price?"
segments.tr: खरीद पूछती है “कीमत क्या है?”

segments.src: Procurement asks "what's the **total cost of ownership**?"
segments.tr: क्रय पूछता है “स्वामित्व की **कुल लागत** (total cost of ownership) क्या है?”

segments.src: Total Cost of Ownership = purchase price
segments.tr: Total Cost of Ownership = purchase price

segments.src: + freight and duties
segments.tr: + freight and duties

segments.src: + inventory carrying cost
segments.tr: + inventory carrying cost

segments.src: + inspection, scrap, and rework
segments.tr: + inspection, scrap, and rework

segments.src: + downtime and expediting
segments.tr: + downtime and expediting

segments.src: + switching or exit costs
segments.tr: + switching or exit costs

segments.src: A part that costs $9.20 instead of $10.00 is not cheaper if it fails inspection twice as often or ships from three weeks farther away.
segments.tr: एक पुर्जा जो $10.00 के बजाय $9.20 का है, वह सस्ता नहीं है यदि वह दो बार अधिक बार निरीक्षण में विफल होता है या तीन सप्ताह दूर से आता है।

segments.src: Not every purchase deserves the same effort.**
segments.tr: हर खरीद को एक जैसे प्रयास की ज़रूरत नहीं होती।**

segments.src: The standard tool here is the **Kraljic matrix**, which sorts everything you buy along two axes: how much money is involved, and how risky the supply is (few suppliers, fragile source, long lead time).
segments.tr: यहाँ का मानक उपकरण **क्रैलजिक मैट्रिक्स** (Kraljic matrix) है, जो आप जो कुछ खरीदते हैं उसे दो अक्षों पर छाँटता है: इसमें कितना पैसा लगा है, और आपूर्ति कितनी जोखिम भरी है (कुछ ही आपूर्तिकर्ता, नाज़ुक स्रोत, लंबा लीड टाइम)।

segments.src: That gives four quadrants, each with a different playbook:
segments.tr: इससे चार चतुर्थांश बनते हैं, प्रत्येक की अपनी अलग रणनीति है:

segments.src: - **Non-critical** (low spend, low risk) — office supplies, cleaning goods. Automate it. Use a catalog, a P-card, and stop thinking about it.
segments.tr: - **गैर-महत्वपूर्ण** (कम खर्च, कम जोखिम) — कार्यालय की आपूर्ति, सफ़ाई का सामान। इसे स्वचालित करें। कैटलॉग, P-card का उपयोग करें, और इसके बारे में सोचना बंद कर दें।

segments.src: - **Leverage** (high spend, low risk) — commodity packaging, standard fasteners. Many capable suppliers want your volume. Compete them, consolidate volume, negotiate hard.
segments.tr: - **लीवरेज** (अधिक खर्च, कम जोखिम) — कमोडिटी पैकेजिंग, मानक फ़ास्टनर। कई सक्षम आपूर्तिकर्ता आपकी मात्रा चाहते हैं। उनके बीच प्रतिस्पर्धा कराएँ, मात्रा को एकत्र करें, और कड़ाई से मोल-भाव करें।

segments.src: - **Bottleneck** (low spend, high risk) — a proprietary sensor, a single certified calibration lab. Small money, big pain if it stops. Hold safety stock, qualify a backup, sign a longer contract.
segments.tr: - **बॉटलनेक** (कम खर्च, अधिक जोखिम) — एक मालिकाना सेंसर, एक एकमात्र प्रमाणित कैलिब्रेशन लैब। पैसा छोटा है, पर रुकने पर बड़ी परेशानी। सुरक्षा स्टॉक रखें, एक बैकअप की पात्रता जाँचें, और लंबा अनुबंध करें।

segments.src: - **Strategic** (high spend, high risk) — the engine, the chip, the signature ingredient. Few alternatives, enormous impact. Build a genuine partnership, share forecasts, invest in the relationship.
segments.tr: - **रणनीतिक** (अधिक खर्च, अधिक जोखिम) — इंजन, चिप, या हस्ताक्षर वाली सामग्री। विकल्प कम हैं, प्रभाव बहुत बड़ा है। एक वास्तविक साझेदारी बनाएँ, पूर्वानुमान साझा करें, और संबंध में निवेश करें।

segments.src: The mistake almost every under-resourced team makes is spending its best people on the wrong quadrant — running competitive bids on paper towels while the sole-source component nobody has a backup for quietly becomes an existential risk.
segments.tr: लगभग हर कम संसाधन वाली टीम जो गलती करती है वह है अपने सबसे अच्छे लोगों को गलत चतुर्थांश पर लगाना — पेपर टावल पर प्रतिस्पर्धी बोलियाँ चलाना, जबकि जिस एकमात्र-स्रोत घटक का कोई बैकअप नहीं है, वह चुपचाप एक अस्तित्वगत जोखिम बन जाता है।

segments.src: Make-or-buy is a strategic choice, not a spreadsheet.**
segments.tr: बनाना-या-खरीदना एक रणनीतिक चुनाव है, स्प्रेडशीट का सवाल नहीं।**

segments.src: Outsourcing tends to win on cost, flexibility, and access to specialized capability.
segments.tr: बाहर से काम करवाना (outsourcing) अक्सर लागत, लचीलापन, और विशेष क्षमता तक पहुँच में जीतता है।

segments.src: Keeping it in-house tends to win on control, quality assurance, IP protection, and responsiveness.
segments.tr: अंदर रखना अक्सर नियंत्रण, गुणवत्ता आश्वासन, IP सुरक्षा, और त्वरित प्रतिक्रिया में जीतता है।

segments.src: The durable rule of thumb: **outsource what is not your core competency, and be extremely careful outsourcing anything a customer would notice.** The catch is that outsourcing doesn't remove risk — it converts execution risk into supplier risk.
segments.tr: टिकाऊ नियम: **जो आपकी मूल दक्षता नहीं है उसे बाहर से करवाएँ, और जो कुछ भी ग्राहक नोटिस कर सकता है उसे बाहर से करवाने में बेहद सावधानी बरतें।** पकड़ यह है कि बाहर से काम करवाने से जोखिम खत्म नहीं होता — यह निष्पादन जोखिम को आपूर्तिकर्ता जोखिम में बदल देता है।

segments.src: Boeing's 787 program is the textbook case: an aggressive outsourcing model spread design and fabrication across a deep global supplier tier, and the resulting integration and coordination problems contributed to years of delay.
segments.tr: Boeing का 787 कार्यक्रम इसका पाठ्यपुस्तक उदाहरण है: एक आक्रामक आउटसोर्सिंग मॉडल ने डिज़ाइन और निर्माण को एक गहरे वैश्विक आपूर्तिकर्ता स्तर में फैला दिया, और इसके परिणामस्वरूप उत्पन्न एकीकरण और समन्वय समस्याओं ने वर्षों की देरी में योगदान दिया।

segments.src: Contracts don't manage relationships.
segments.tr: अनुबंध संबंधों का प्रबंधन नहीं करते।

segments.src: People do.**
segments.tr: लोग करते हैं।**

segments.src: **Supplier Relationship Management (SRM)** is the practice of segmenting suppliers, scoring them on real metrics, and investing management attention where it pays off.
segments.tr: **आपूर्तिकर्ता संबंध प्रबंधन (SRM)** आपूर्तिकर्ताओं को वर्गीकृत करने, उन्हें वास्तविक मापदंडों पर अंक देने, और प्रबंधन का ध्यान वहाँ लगाने की प्रथा है जहाँ उसका फल मिले।

segments.src: A typical scorecard runs on **QCDS** — quality (defect rate, PPM), cost (price trend, cost-reduction ideas), delivery (on-time-in-full percentage), and service (responsiveness, technical support).
segments.tr: एक विशिष्ट स्कोरकार्ड **QCDS** पर चलता है — गुणवत्ता (दोष दर, PPM), लागत (मूल्य प्रवृत्ति, लागत-कटौती के विचार), डिलीवरी (समय पर-पूरी-मात्रा प्रतिशत), और सेवा (त्वरित प्रतिक्रिया, तकनीकी सहायता)।

segments.src: You cannot run a deep partnership with 4,000 suppliers, and you shouldn't try.
segments.tr: आप 4,000 आपूर्तिकर्ताओं के साथ गहरी साझेदारी नहीं चला सकते, और आपको कोशिश भी नहीं करनी चाहिए।

segments.src: You run transactional discipline with most of them, preferred-supplier terms with a couple hundred, and true joint development with the handful that determine whether your product is any good.
segments.tr: अधिकांश के साथ आप लेन-देन का अनुशासन चलाते हैं, कुछ सौ के साथ पसंदीदा-आपूर्तिकर्ता शर्तें, और उन चंद के साथ वास्तविक संयुक्त विकास जो तय करते हैं कि आपका उत्पाद अच्छा है या नहीं।

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## रोज़मर्रा की ज़िंदगी में

segments.src: Say you run **Trailhead Coffee**, a nine-location café chain in Austin.
segments.tr: मान लीजिए आप **Trailhead Coffee** चलाते हैं, ऑस्टिन में नौ स्थानों वाली एक कैफ़े श्रृंखला।

segments.src: Annual revenue is $6.2 million, net margin about 5%, and roughly $2.4 million a year goes out the door to suppliers.
segments.tr: वार्षिक राजस्व $6.2 मिलियन है, शुद्ध मार्जिन लगभग 5% है, और हर साल लगभग $2.4 मिलियन आपूर्तिकर्ताओं को जाता है।

segments.src: Your buying list sorts itself into the quadrants almost immediately.
segments.tr: आपकी खरीद सूची लगभग तुरंत चतुर्थांशों में अपने आप छँट जाती है।

segments.src: **Green coffee beans — strategic.** Around $520,000 a year, and your entire brand rests on it.
segments.tr: **ग्रीन कॉफ़ी बीन्स — रणनीतिक।** लगभग $520,000 प्रति वर्ष, और आपका पूरा ब्रांड इसी पर टिका है।

segments.src: There is no interchangeable substitute; customers can taste a switch.
segments.tr: कोई विनिमेय विकल्प नहीं है; ग्राहक बदलाव का स्वाद पहचान लेते हैं।

segments.src: So you don't run this on an annual bid.
segments.tr: तो आप इसे वार्षिक बोली से नहीं चलाते।

segments.src: You sign a multi-year agreement with your Chiapas importer, visit the co-op, share your growth forecast so they can plan their crop, and accept that you'll pay a little more for consistency and first call on the good lots.
segments.tr: आप अपने Chiapas आयातक के साथ बहु-वर्षीय समझौता करते हैं, सहकारी समिति का दौरा करते हैं, अपना विकास पूर्वानुमान साझा करते हैं ताकि वे अपनी फ़सल की योजना बना सकें, और स्थिरता व अच्छे लॉट्स पर पहले अधिकार के लिए थोड़ा अधिक भुगतान स्वीकार करते हैं।

segments.src: **Cups, lids, and sleeves — leverage.** About $310,000 a year, and a dozen distributors in Texas would love the business.
segments.tr: **कप, ढक्कन और स्लीव — लीवरेज।** लगभग $310,000 प्रति वर्ष, और टेक्सास में एक दर्जन वितरक यह व्यवसाय पाने को उत्सुक हैं।

segments.src: This is where a competitive RFQ pays.
segments.tr: यहीं प्रतिस्पर्धी RFQ काम आता है।

segments.src: You consolidate all nine stores onto one contract instead of letting each manager order locally, and you land 9% off — roughly $28,000.
segments.tr: आप सभी नौ दुकानों को एक ही अनुबंध पर समेकित करते हैं, बजाय इसके कि हर प्रबंधक स्थानीय स्तर पर ऑर्डर करे, और आपको 9% की छूट मिलती है — लगभग $28,000।

segments.src: **Espresso machine service — bottleneck.** Maybe $18,000 a year.
segments.tr: **एस्प्रेसो मशीन सेवा — बॉटलनेक।** शायद $18,000 प्रति वर्ष।

segments.src: Trivial money.
segments.tr: तुच्छ राशि।

segments.src: But exactly one certified tech in the metro services your machines, and if a grouphead fails on a Saturday at your busiest store, you lose $2,800 in a day.
segments.tr: पर महानगर में ठीक एक प्रमाणित तकनीशियन आपकी मशीनें सर्विस करता है, और अगर आपकी सबसे व्यस्त दुकान पर शनिवार को एक ग्रुपहेड खराब हो जाए, तो एक दिन में $2,800 का नुकसान होता है।

segments.src: So you pay for a service contract with a guaranteed four-hour response, and you keep a spare set of critical parts on the shelf.
segments.tr: तो आप गारंटीड चार-घंटे प्रतिक्रिया वाला सेवा अनुबंध भुगतान करते हैं, और महत्वपूर्ण पुर्जों का एक अतिरिक्त सेट शेल्फ़ पर रखते हैं।

segments.src: Small spend, deliberate attention.
segments.tr: कम खर्च, सोच-समझकर ध्यान।

segments.src: **Office and cleaning supplies — non-critical.** Around $40,000.
segments.tr: **कार्यालय और सफ़ाई आपूर्ति — गैर-महत्वपूर्ण।** लगभग $40,000।

segments.src: Put it on a punch-out catalog with one distributor, give managers a spending limit, and never hold a meeting about it again.
segments.tr: इसे एक विक्रेता के साथ पंच-आउट कैटलॉग पर डालें, प्रबंधकों को खर्च की सीमा दें, और इस पर फिर कभी बैठक न करें।

segments.src: Now the part that makes the CFO sit up.
segments.tr: अब वह हिस्सा जो CFO को सीधा कर देता है।

segments.src: That $28,000 saved on cups is $28,000 of pure operating profit.
segments.tr: कप पर बचाए गए $28,000 मतलब $28,000 शुद्ध परिचालन लाभ।

segments.src: To generate the same $28,000 through sales at a 5% net margin, you'd have to sell **$560,000** more coffee — roughly a tenth of the entire business.
segments.tr: 5% शुद्ध मार्जिन पर बिक्री के ज़रिए वही $28,000 कमाने के लिए, आपको **$560,000** अधिक कॉफ़ी बेचनी होगी — यानी पूरे व्यवसाय का लगभग दसवाँ हिस्सा।

segments.src: That's the **profit-leverage effect**, and it's why procurement is one of the highest-return functions in a company that nobody outside the building ever thinks about.
segments.tr: यही **लाभ-लीवरेज प्रभाव** (profit-leverage effect) है, और इसीलिए क्रय एक ऐसा सर्वाधिक-प्रतिफल देने वाला कार्य है जिसके बारे में इमारत के बाहर कोई कभी नहीं सोचता।

segments.src: The catch: chase that saving into the wrong quadrant — switch to a cheaper green coffee supplier to save $30,000 — and you may lose regulars who never tell you why they stopped coming.
segments.tr: पकड़ यह है: उस बचत के पीछे गलत चतुर्थांश में भागें — $30,000 बचाने के लिए सस्ते ग्रीन कॉफ़ी आपूर्तिकर्ता पर स्विच करें — और आप उन नियमित ग्राहकों को खो सकते हैं जो कभी नहीं बताते कि उन्होंने आना क्यों बंद किया।

segments.src: Savings that damage the product aren't savings.
segments.tr: जो बचत उत्पाद को नुकसान पहुँचाती है, वह बचत नहीं है।

segments.src: ## 3-Line Recap
1. Purchasing pays invoices; procurement decides what to buy, from whom, and on what terms — judged on total cost of ownership, not sticker price.
segments.tr: 1. खरीद इनवॉइस चुकाती है; क्रय तय करता है क्या खरीदना है, किससे, और किन शर्तों पर — जिसका मूल्यांकन स्वामित्व की कुल लागत पर होता है, न कि स्टिकर मूल्य पर।

segments.src: 2. Segment your spend (Kraljic: non-critical, leverage, bottleneck, strategic) and match your effort to the quadrant, because uniform effort wastes it.
segments.tr: 2. अपने खर्च को वर्गीकृत करें (क्रैलजिक: गैर-महत्वपूर्ण, लीवरेज, बॉटलनेक, रणनीतिक) और अपने प्रयास को चतुर्थांश के अनुरूप रखें, क्योंकि एक समान प्रयास बर्बाद होता है।

segments.src: 3. Outsourcing converts execution risk into supplier risk, so SRM — scorecards, segmentation, real relationships — is what keeps the savings from turning into an outage.
segments.tr: 3. बाहर से काम करवाने से निष्पादन जोखिम आपूर्तिकर्ता जोखिम में बदल जाता है, इसलिए SRM — स्कोरकार्ड, वर्गीकरण, वास्तविक संबंध — ही वह चीज़ है जो बचत को आउटेज में बदलने से रोकती है।

segments.src: ## ✅ Self-Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ स्व-प्रश्नोत्तरी

segments.src: **1.** A component costs very little each year, but only one certified supplier in the world makes it and a stoppage would halt your line.
segments.tr: **1.** एक घटक हर वर्ष बहुत कम लागत का है, लेकिन दुनिया में केवल एक प्रमाणित आपूर्तिकर्ता इसे बनाता है, और इसके रुकने से आपकी लाइन ठप हो जाएगी।

segments.src: In the Kraljic matrix, this is:
segments.tr: क्रैलजिक मैट्रिक्स में यह है:

segments.src: - (A) Non-critical
segments.tr: - (A) गैर-महत्वपूर्ण

segments.src: - (B) Leverage
segments.tr: - (B) लीवरेज

segments.src: - (C) Bottleneck
segments.tr: - (C) बॉटलनेक

segments.src: - (D) Strategic
segments.tr: - (D) रणनीतिक

segments.src: **2.** True or False: A company with a 4% net profit margin that cuts $100,000 from its purchasing costs achieves the same profit impact as generating $100,000 in additional sales.
segments.tr: **2.** सही या गलत: 4% शुद्ध लाभ मार्जिन वाली कंपनी जो अपनी खरीद लागत से $100,000 कम करती है, वह $100,000 की अतिरिक्त बिक्री करने जितना ही लाभ प्रभाव प्राप्त करती है।

segments.src: **3.** Which of these is the best description of Total Cost of Ownership?
segments.tr: **3.** स्वामित्व की कुल लागत (TCO) का सबसे अच्छा वर्णन इनमें से कौन-सा है?

segments.src: - (A) The unit price plus sales tax
segments.tr: - (A) इकाई मूल्य और बिक्री कर

segments.src: - (B) The purchase price plus all downstream costs of using that item, including freight, carrying cost, quality failures, and downtime
segments.tr: - (B) खरीद मूल्य के साथ उस वस्तु के उपयोग की सभी बाद की लागतें, जिनमें माल ढुलाई, भंडारण लागत, गुणवत्ता विफलताएँ, और डाउनटाइम शामिल हैं

segments.src: - (C) The total dollar value of all purchase orders issued in a year
segments.tr: - (C) एक वर्ष में जारी सभी खरीद आदेशों का कुल डॉलर मूल्य

segments.src: - (D) The supplier's manufacturing cost plus their profit margin
segments.tr: - (D) आपूर्तिकर्ता की विनिर्माण लागत + उनका लाभ मार्जिन

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 आज के शब्द

segments.src: - **Procurement** — The end-to-end process of identifying needs, sourcing and qualifying suppliers, contracting, buying, and managing supplier performance.
segments.tr: - **क्रय (Procurement)** — ज़रूरतें पहचानने, आपूर्तिकर्ताओं को खोजने और परखने, अनुबंध करने, खरीदने, और आपूर्तिकर्ता प्रदर्शन के प्रबंधन की शुरू से अंत तक की प्रक्रिया।

segments.src: - **Total Cost of Ownership (TCO)** — The full cost of acquiring and using a purchased item, including freight, inventory carrying, quality failures, downtime, and switching costs — not just the price.
segments.tr: - **स्वामित्व की कुल लागत (TCO)** — किसी खरीदी गई वस्तु को प्राप्त करने और उपयोग करने की पूरी लागत, जिसमें माल ढुलाई, इन्वेंटरी भंडारण, गुणवत्ता विफलताएँ, डाउनटाइम, और स्विचिंग लागत शामिल हैं — केवल कीमत नहीं।

segments.src: - **Kraljic Matrix** — A spend-segmentation framework plotting purchases by financial impact and supply risk into four quadrants (non-critical, leverage, bottleneck, strategic), each with its own sourcing strategy.
segments.tr: - **क्रैलजिक मैट्रिक्स (Kraljic Matrix)** — एक खर्च-वर्गीकरण ढाँचा जो खरीद को वित्तीय प्रभाव और आपूर्ति जोखिम के आधार पर चार चतुर्थांशों (गैर-महत्वपूर्ण, लीवरेज, बॉटलनेक, रणनीतिक) में रखता है, प्रत्येक की अपनी सोर्सिंग रणनीति के साथ।

segments.src: - **Supplier Relationship Management (SRM)** — Segmenting the supply base and systematically managing performance and collaboration, concentrating attention on the suppliers that most affect the business.
segments.tr: - **आपूर्तिकर्ता संबंध प्रबंधन (SRM)** — आपूर्ति आधार को वर्गीकृत करना और प्रदर्शन व सहयोग का व्यवस्थित प्रबंधन करना, उन आपूर्तिकर्ताओं पर ध्यान केंद्रित करते हुए जो व्यवसाय को सबसे अधिक प्रभावित करते हैं।

segments.src: - **Profit-Leverage Effect** — The principle that a dollar saved in purchasing raises operating profit by roughly a full dollar, while a dollar of new sales raises it only by the margin rate.
segments.tr: - **लाभ-लीवरेज प्रभाव (Profit-Leverage Effect)** — यह सिद्धांत कि खरीद में बचाया गया एक डॉलर परिचालन लाभ को लगभग पूरे एक डॉलर तक बढ़ाता है, जबकि नई बिक्री का एक डॉलर उसे केवल मार्जिन दर तक बढ़ाता है।

segments.src: *Answers: **1 — (C) Bottleneck.** Low spend but high supply risk.
segments.tr: *उत्तर: **1 — (C) बॉटलनेक।** कम खर्च, पर उच्च आपूर्ति जोखिम।

segments.src: The correct response isn't hard negotiation (there's no leverage at that volume) but risk mitigation: safety stock, a qualified second source, and a longer-term contract.*
segments.tr: सही प्रतिक्रिया कठोर मोल-भाव नहीं है (उस मात्रा पर कोई लीवरेज नहीं है) बल्कि जोखिम शमन है: सुरक्षा स्टॉक, एक प्रमाणित दूसरा स्रोत, और लंबी-अवधि का अनुबंध।*

segments.src: ***2 — False.** It's dramatically better.
segments.tr: ***2 — गलत।** यह नाटकीय रूप से बेहतर है।

segments.src: At a 4% margin, $100,000 in additional sales yields about $4,000 of profit, while $100,000 in purchasing savings drops close to the full $100,000 to the bottom line — you'd need roughly $2.5 million in new sales to match it.
segments.tr: 4% मार्जिन पर, $100,000 की अतिरिक्त बिक्री लगभग $4,000 का लाभ देती है, जबकि $100,000 की खरीद बचत लगभग पूरे $100,000 को सीधे लाभ में जोड़ती है — उसकी बराबरी के लिए आपको लगभग $2.5 मिलियन की नई बिक्री चाहिए होगी।

segments.src: That's the profit-leverage effect.*
segments.tr: यही लाभ-लीवरेज प्रभाव है।*

segments.src: ***3 — (B).** TCO captures everything the item costs you over its life, not just the invoice.
segments.tr: ***3 — (B).** TCO वह सब कुछ समेटता है जो वह वस्तु आपको उसके जीवनकाल में लागत देती है, केवल इनवॉइस नहीं।

segments.src: It's the reason the lowest bid frequently loses on a properly built evaluation.*
segments.tr: यही कारण है कि उचित रूप से बनाए गए मूल्यांकन में सबसे कम बोली अक्सर हार जाती है।*

es.title: [Logistics 101 #6] Cada dólar que no gastas es un dólar que no tienes que ganar

segments.src: > Procurement is the discipline of deciding what to buy, who to buy it from, and how to keep that relationship working — and because purchased goods and services are the single largest line item in most companies, a dollar saved there lands on the profit line far faster than a dollar chased through sales.
segments.tr: > El abastecimiento es la disciplina de decidir qué comprar, a quién comprárselo y cómo mantener funcionando esa relación. Y como los bienes y servicios comprados son la partida más grande en la mayoría de las empresas, un dólar ahorrado ahí llega a la utilidad mucho más rápido que un dólar perseguido mediante ventas.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Concepto de hoy

segments.src: Ask most people what a company does and they'll describe what it sells.
segments.tr: Pregunta a casi cualquiera qué hace una empresa y te describirá lo que vende.

segments.src: But look at the income statement of almost any manufacturer, retailer, or restaurant group and you'll find the same thing: the biggest number isn't payroll or rent.
segments.tr: Pero revisa el estado de resultados de casi cualquier fabricante, minorista o grupo de restaurantes y encontrarás lo mismo: la cifra más grande no es la nómina ni el alquiler.

segments.src: It's what the company **bought** — raw materials, components, packaging, freight, contract services.
segments.tr: Es lo que la empresa **compró**: materias primas, componentes, empaques, fletes y servicios contratados.

segments.src: In many manufacturing firms, purchased goods and services eat more than half of every sales dollar.
segments.tr: En muchas empresas manufactureras, los bienes y servicios comprados absorben más de la mitad de cada dólar de ventas.

segments.src: That's why procurement matters, and why it's the sixth stop in this series.
segments.tr: Por eso importa el abastecimiento, y por eso es la sexta parada de esta serie.

segments.src: Here are the four ideas that hold it together.
segments.tr: Estas son las cuatro ideas que lo sostienen.

segments.src: Purchasing is a transaction.
segments.tr: Comprar es una transacción.

segments.src: Procurement is a strategy.**
segments.tr: Abastecerse es una estrategia.**

segments.src: Purchasing is the narrow act of issuing a purchase order and paying the invoice.
segments.tr: Comprar es el acto puntual de emitir una orden de compra y pagar la factura.

segments.src: Procurement is the whole arc around it: figuring out what the business actually needs, deciding whether to make it in-house or buy it, finding and qualifying suppliers, negotiating terms, and managing performance for years afterward.
segments.tr: Abastecerse es todo el recorrido alrededor: determinar qué necesita realmente el negocio, decidir si lo fabrica internamente o lo compra, encontrar y calificar proveedores, negociar condiciones y gestionar su desempeño durante años.

segments.src: Purchasing asks "what's the price?"
segments.tr: Comprar pregunta "¿cuál es el precio?".

segments.src: Procurement asks "what's the **total cost of ownership**?"
segments.tr: Abastecerse pregunta "¿cuál es el **costo total de propiedad**?"

segments.src: Total Cost of Ownership = purchase price
segments.tr: Total Cost of Ownership = purchase price

segments.src: + freight and duties
segments.tr: + freight and duties

segments.src: + inventory carrying cost
segments.tr: + inventory carrying cost

segments.src: + inspection, scrap, and rework
segments.tr: + inspection, scrap, and rework

segments.src: + downtime and expediting
segments.tr: + downtime and expediting

segments.src: + switching or exit costs
segments.tr: + switching or exit costs

segments.src: A part that costs $9.20 instead of $10.00 is not cheaper if it fails inspection twice as often or ships from three weeks farther away.
segments.tr: Una pieza que cuesta $9.20 en lugar de $10.00 no es más barata si falla la inspección el doble de veces o si viene de tres semanas más lejos.

segments.src: Not every purchase deserves the same effort.**
segments.tr: No toda compra merece el mismo esfuerzo.**

segments.src: The standard tool here is the **Kraljic matrix**, which sorts everything you buy along two axes: how much money is involved, and how risky the supply is (few suppliers, fragile source, long lead time).
segments.tr: La herramienta estándar aquí es la **matriz de Kraljic**, que clasifica todo lo que compras según dos ejes: cuánto dinero está en juego y qué tan riesgoso es el suministro (pocos proveedores, origen frágil, tiempo de entrega largo).

segments.src: That gives four quadrants, each with a different playbook:
segments.tr: Eso produce cuatro cuadrantes, cada uno con una estrategia distinta:

segments.src: - **Non-critical** (low spend, low risk) — office supplies, cleaning goods. Automate it. Use a catalog, a P-card, and stop thinking about it.
segments.tr: - **No crítico** (gasto bajo, riesgo bajo): útiles de oficina y productos de limpieza. Automatízalo. Usa un catálogo, una tarjeta de compra y deja de pensar en ello.

segments.src: - **Leverage** (high spend, low risk) — commodity packaging, standard fasteners. Many capable suppliers want your volume. Compete them, consolidate volume, negotiate hard.
segments.tr: - **Palanca** (gasto alto, riesgo bajo): empaques básicos, sujetadores estándar. Muchos proveedores capaces quieren tu volumen. Haz que compitan, consolida volumen y negocia con firmeza.

segments.src: - **Bottleneck** (low spend, high risk) — a proprietary sensor, a single certified calibration lab. Small money, big pain if it stops. Hold safety stock, qualify a backup, sign a longer contract.
segments.tr: - **Cuello de botella** (gasto bajo, riesgo alto): un sensor propietario, un único laboratorio certificado de calibración. Poco dinero, gran dolor si se detiene. Mantén inventario de seguridad, califica un respaldo y firma un contrato más largo.

segments.src: - **Strategic** (high spend, high risk) — the engine, the chip, the signature ingredient. Few alternatives, enormous impact. Build a genuine partnership, share forecasts, invest in the relationship.
segments.tr: - **Estratégico** (gasto alto, riesgo alto): el motor, el chip, el ingrediente característico. Pocas alternativas, impacto enorme. Construye una alianza genuina, comparte pronósticos e invierte en la relación.

segments.src: The mistake almost every under-resourced team makes is spending its best people on the wrong quadrant — running competitive bids on paper towels while the sole-source component nobody has a backup for quietly becomes an existential risk.
segments.tr: El error que casi todos los equipos con pocos recursos cometen es dedicar a su mejor gente al cuadrante equivocado: hacer licitaciones competitivas para toallas de papel mientras el componente de fuente única, sin respaldo, se convierte silenciosamente en un riesgo existencial.

segments.src: Make-or-buy is a strategic choice, not a spreadsheet.**
segments.tr: Fabricar o comprar es una decisión estratégica, no una hoja de cálculo.**

segments.src: Outsourcing tends to win on cost, flexibility, and access to specialized capability.
segments.tr: La tercerización suele ganar en costo, flexibilidad y acceso a capacidades especializadas.

segments.src: Keeping it in-house tends to win on control, quality assurance, IP protection, and responsiveness.
segments.tr: Mantenerla internamente suele ganar en control, aseguramiento de calidad, protección de propiedad intelectual y capacidad de respuesta.

segments.src: The durable rule of thumb: **outsource what is not your core competency, and be extremely careful outsourcing anything a customer would notice.** The catch is that outsourcing doesn't remove risk — it converts execution risk into supplier risk.
segments.tr: La regla práctica duradera: **terceriza lo que no es tu competencia central, y ten mucho cuidado al tercerizar cualquier cosa que un cliente notaría.** El detalle es que tercerizar no elimina el riesgo: lo convierte en riesgo de proveedor.

segments.src: Boeing's 787 program is the textbook case: an aggressive outsourcing model spread design and fabrication across a deep global supplier tier, and the resulting integration and coordination problems contributed to years of delay.
segments.tr: El programa del 787 de Boeing es el caso de libro: un modelo de tercerización agresivo repartió el diseño y la fabricación entre una amplia red global de proveedores, y los problemas de integración y coordinación que surgieron contribuyeron a años de retraso.

segments.src: Contracts don't manage relationships.
segments.tr: Los contratos no gestionan relaciones.

segments.src: People do.**
segments.tr: Las personas sí.**

segments.src: **Supplier Relationship Management (SRM)** is the practice of segmenting suppliers, scoring them on real metrics, and investing management attention where it pays off.
segments.tr: La **gestión de la relación con proveedores (SRM)** es la práctica de segmentar proveedores, evaluarlos con métricas reales e invertir la atención gerencial donde rinde.

segments.src: A typical scorecard runs on **QCDS** — quality (defect rate, PPM), cost (price trend, cost-reduction ideas), delivery (on-time-in-full percentage), and service (responsiveness, technical support).
segments.tr: Una tarjeta de evaluación típica se basa en **QCDS**: calidad (tasa de defectos, PPM), costo (tendencia de precios, ideas de reducción de costos), entrega (porcentaje de entregas completas a tiempo) y servicio (capacidad de respuesta, soporte técnico).

segments.src: You cannot run a deep partnership with 4,000 suppliers, and you shouldn't try.
segments.tr: No puedes mantener una alianza profunda con 4,000 proveedores, y no deberías intentarlo.

segments.src: You run transactional discipline with most of them, preferred-supplier terms with a couple hundred, and true joint development with the handful that determine whether your product is any good.
segments.tr: Mantienes disciplina transaccional con la mayoría, condiciones de proveedor preferente con un par de cientos, y desarrollo conjunto real con el puñado que determina si tu producto es bueno.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## En la vida cotidiana

segments.src: Say you run **Trailhead Coffee**, a nine-location café chain in Austin.
segments.tr: Imagina que diriges **Trailhead Coffee**, una cadena de cafeterías con nueve locales en Austin.

segments.src: Annual revenue is $6.2 million, net margin about 5%, and roughly $2.4 million a year goes out the door to suppliers.
segments.tr: Los ingresos anuales son de $6.2 millones, el margen neto ronda el 5% y unos $2.4 millones al año salen hacia proveedores.

segments.src: Your buying list sorts itself into the quadrants almost immediately.
segments.tr: Tu lista de compras se clasifica sola en los cuadrantes casi de inmediato.

segments.src: **Green coffee beans — strategic.** Around $520,000 a year, and your entire brand rests on it.
segments.tr: **Granos de café verde: estratégico.** Alrededor de $520,000 al año, y toda tu marca descansa en ellos.

segments.src: There is no interchangeable substitute; customers can taste a switch.
segments.tr: No hay un sustituto intercambiable; los clientes notan un cambio.

segments.src: So you don't run this on an annual bid.
segments.tr: Por eso no lo manejas con una licitación anual.

segments.src: You sign a multi-year agreement with your Chiapas importer, visit the co-op, share your growth forecast so they can plan their crop, and accept that you'll pay a little more for consistency and first call on the good lots.
segments.tr: Firmas un acuerdo plurianual con tu importador de Chiapas, visitas la cooperativa, compartes tu pronóstico de crecimiento para que puedan planificar su cosecha, y aceptas pagar un poco más a cambio de consistencia y prioridad en los mejores lotes.

segments.src: **Cups, lids, and sleeves — leverage.** About $310,000 a year, and a dozen distributors in Texas would love the business.
segments.tr: **Vasos, tapas y mangas: palanca.** Unos $310,000 al año, y una docena de distribuidores en Texas querrían el negocio.

segments.src: This is where a competitive RFQ pays.
segments.tr: Aquí una cotización competitiva (RFQ) rinde frutos.

segments.src: You consolidate all nine stores onto one contract instead of letting each manager order locally, and you land 9% off — roughly $28,000.
segments.tr: Consolidas los nueve locales en un solo contrato en lugar de dejar que cada gerente pida localmente, y obtienes 9% de descuento: aproximadamente $28,000.

segments.src: **Espresso machine service — bottleneck.** Maybe $18,000 a year.
segments.tr: **Servicio de la máquina de espresso: cuello de botella.** Quizá $18,000 al año.

segments.src: Trivial money.
segments.tr: Dinero insignificante.

segments.src: But exactly one certified tech in the metro services your machines, and if a grouphead fails on a Saturday at your busiest store, you lose $2,800 in a day.
segments.tr: Pero hay exactamente un técnico certificado en el área metropolitana que da servicio a tus máquinas, y si un grupo falla un sábado en tu local más concurrido, pierdes $2,800 en un día.

segments.src: So you pay for a service contract with a guaranteed four-hour response, and you keep a spare set of critical parts on the shelf.
segments.tr: Así que pagas un contrato de servicio con respuesta garantizada en cuatro horas, y mantienes un juego de repuestos críticos en el estante.

segments.src: Small spend, deliberate attention.
segments.tr: Gasto pequeño, atención deliberada.

segments.src: **Office and cleaning supplies — non-critical.** Around $40,000.
segments.tr: **Suministros de oficina y limpieza: no crítico.** Alrededor de $40,000.

segments.src: Put it on a punch-out catalog with one distributor, give managers a spending limit, and never hold a meeting about it again.
segments.tr: Ponlos en un catálogo de compra directa con un solo distribuidor, da a los gerentes un límite de gasto y no vuelvas a tener una reunión sobre esto.

segments.src: Now the part that makes the CFO sit up.
segments.tr: Ahora viene la parte que hace que el director financiero se incorpore en su silla.

segments.src: That $28,000 saved on cups is $28,000 of pure operating profit.
segments.tr: Esos $28,000 ahorrados en vasos son $28,000 de utilidad operativa pura.

segments.src: To generate the same $28,000 through sales at a 5% net margin, you'd have to sell **$560,000** more coffee — roughly a tenth of the entire business.
segments.tr: Para generar los mismos $28,000 por ventas con un margen neto del 5%, tendrías que vender **$560,000** más de café: aproximadamente una décima parte de todo el negocio.

segments.src: That's the **profit-leverage effect**, and it's why procurement is one of the highest-return functions in a company that nobody outside the building ever thinks about.
segments.tr: Ese es el **efecto de apalancamiento sobre la utilidad**, y por eso el abastecimiento es una de las funciones de mayor rendimiento en una empresa, aunque nadie fuera del edificio jamás piense en ella.

segments.src: The catch: chase that saving into the wrong quadrant — switch to a cheaper green coffee supplier to save $30,000 — and you may lose regulars who never tell you why they stopped coming.
segments.tr: La trampa: si persigues ese ahorro en el cuadrante equivocado (cambiar a un proveedor de café verde más barato para ahorrar $30,000), podrías perder clientes habituales que nunca te dirán por qué dejaron de venir.

segments.src: Savings that damage the product aren't savings.
segments.tr: Los ahorros que dañan el producto no son ahorros.

segments.src: ## 3-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## Resumen en 3 líneas

segments.src: 1. Purchasing pays invoices; procurement decides what to buy, from whom, and on what terms — judged on total cost of ownership, not sticker price.
segments.tr: 1. Comprar paga facturas; abastecerse decide qué comprar, a quién y en qué condiciones, juzgado por el costo total de propiedad y no por el precio de etiqueta.

segments.src: 2. Segment your spend (Kraljic: non-critical, leverage, bottleneck, strategic) and match your effort to the quadrant, because uniform effort wastes it.
segments.tr: 2. Segmenta tu gasto (Kraljic: no crítico, palanca, cuello de botella, estratégico) y ajusta tu esfuerzo al cuadrante, porque un esfuerzo uniforme lo desperdicia.

segments.src: 3. Outsourcing converts execution risk into supplier risk, so SRM — scorecards, segmentation, real relationships — is what keeps the savings from turning into an outage.
segments.tr: 3. La tercerización convierte el riesgo de ejecución en riesgo de proveedor, así que el SRM (tarjetas de evaluación, segmentación, relaciones reales) es lo que evita que los ahorros se conviertan en una interrupción.

segments.tr: ## ✅ Autoevaluación

segments.tr: **1.** Un componente cuesta muy poco cada año, pero solo un proveedor certificado en el mundo lo fabrica, y una detención pararía tu línea.

segments.tr: En la matriz de Kraljic, esto corresponde a:

segments.tr: - (A) No crítico

segments.tr: - (B) Palanca

segments.src: **2.** True or False: A company with a 4% net profit margin that cuts $100,000 from its purchasing costs achieves the same profit impact as generating $100,000 in additional sales.
segments.tr: **2.** Verdadero o falso: una empresa con un margen neto del 4% que reduce $100,000 de sus costos de compra logra el mismo impacto en utilidades que generar $100,000 en ventas adicionales.

segments.src: **3.** Which of these is the best description of Total Cost of Ownership?
segments.tr: **3.** ¿Cuál de estas es la mejor descripción del Costo Total de Propiedad?

segments.src: - (A) The unit price plus sales tax
segments.tr: - (A) El precio unitario más el impuesto sobre ventas

segments.src: - (B) The purchase price plus all downstream costs of using that item, including freight, carrying cost, quality failures, and downtime
segments.tr: - (B) El precio de compra más todos los costos posteriores de usar ese artículo, incluidos el flete, el costo de mantenimiento de inventario, las fallas de calidad y el tiempo de inactividad

segments.src: - (C) The total dollar value of all purchase orders issued in a year
segments.tr: - (C) El valor monetario total de todas las órdenes de compra emitidas en un año

segments.src: - (D) The supplier's manufacturing cost plus their profit margin
segments.tr: - (D) El costo de fabricación del proveedor más su margen de utilidad

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Términos de hoy

segments.src: - **Procurement** — The end-to-end process of identifying needs, sourcing and qualifying suppliers, contracting, buying, and managing supplier performance.
segments.tr: - **Abastecimiento (procurement)**: el proceso de principio a fin para identificar necesidades, buscar y calificar proveedores, contratar, comprar y gestionar el desempeño de los proveedores.

segments.src: - **Total Cost of Ownership (TCO)** — The full cost of acquiring and using a purchased item, including freight, inventory carrying, quality failures, downtime, and switching costs — not just the price.
segments.tr: - **Costo Total de Propiedad (TCO)**: el costo completo de adquirir y usar un artículo comprado, incluidos el flete, el costo de mantener inventario, las fallas de calidad, el tiempo de inactividad y los costos de cambio, no solo el precio.

segments.src: - **Kraljic Matrix** — A spend-segmentation framework plotting purchases by financial impact and supply risk into four quadrants (non-critical, leverage, bottleneck, strategic), each with its own sourcing strategy.
segments.tr: - **Matriz de Kraljic**: un marco de segmentación del gasto que ubica las compras según su impacto financiero y su riesgo de suministro en cuatro cuadrantes (no crítico, palanca, cuello de botella, estratégico), cada uno con su propia estrategia de abastecimiento.

segments.src: - **Supplier Relationship Management (SRM)** — Segmenting the supply base and systematically managing performance and collaboration, concentrating attention on the suppliers that most affect the business.
segments.tr: - **Gestión de la relación con proveedores (SRM)**: segmentar la base de proveedores y gestionar sistemáticamente su desempeño y colaboración, concentrando la atención en los proveedores que más afectan al negocio.

segments.src: - **Profit-Leverage Effect** — The principle that a dollar saved in purchasing raises operating profit by roughly a full dollar, while a dollar of new sales raises it only by the margin rate.
segments.tr: - **Efecto de apalancamiento sobre la utilidad**: el principio de que un dólar ahorrado en compras aumenta la utilidad operativa aproximadamente un dólar completo, mientras que un dólar de ventas nuevas la aumenta solo en la tasa de margen.

segments.src: *Answers: **1 — (C) Bottleneck.** Low spend but high supply risk.
segments.tr: *Respuestas: **1 — (C) Cuello de botella.** Gasto bajo pero alto riesgo de suministro.

segments.src: The correct response isn't hard negotiation (there's no leverage at that volume) but risk mitigation: safety stock, a qualified second source, and a longer-term contract.*
segments.tr: La respuesta correcta no es la negociación dura (no hay palanca con ese volumen), sino la mitigación de riesgos: inventario de seguridad, una segunda fuente calificada y un contrato de mayor plazo.*

segments.src: ***2 — False.** It's dramatically better.
segments.tr: ***2 — Falso.** Es mucho mejor.

segments.src: At a 4% margin, $100,000 in additional sales yields about $4,000 of profit, while $100,000 in purchasing savings drops close to the full $100,000 to the bottom line — you'd need roughly $2.5 million in new sales to match it.
segments.tr: Con un margen del 4%, $100,000 en ventas adicionales generan unos $4,000 de utilidad, mientras que $100,000 en ahorros de compra pasan casi íntegros a la utilidad: necesitarías unos $2.5 millones en ventas nuevas para igualarlo.

segments.src: That's the profit-leverage effect.*
segments.tr: Ese es el efecto de apalancamiento sobre la utilidad.*

segments.src: ***3 — (B).** TCO captures everything the item costs you over its life, not just the invoice.
segments.tr: ***3 — (B).** El TCO incluye todo lo que el artículo te cuesta a lo largo de su vida útil, no solo la factura.

segments.src: It's the reason the lowest bid frequently loses on a properly built evaluation.*
segments.tr: Es la razón por la que la oferta más baja con frecuencia pierde en una evaluación bien construida.*

ar.title: [Logistics 101 #6] كل دولار لا تنفقه هو دولار لا تحتاج إلى كسبه

segments.src: > Procurement is the discipline of deciding what to buy, who to buy it from, and how to keep that relationship working — and because purchased goods and services are the single largest line item in most companies, a dollar saved there lands on the profit line far faster than a dollar chased through sales.
segments.tr: > تُعنى إدارة المشتريات بتحديد ما يجب شراؤه، ومن أين يُشترى، وكيفية الحفاظ على حسن سير هذه العلاقة. ولأن السلع والخدمات المشتراة هي البند الأكبر في معظم الشركات، فإن الدولار الذي يُوفَّر هنا يصل إلى صافي الربح أسرع بكثير من الدولار الذي يُلاحَق عبر المبيعات.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## مفهوم اليوم

segments.src: Ask most people what a company does and they'll describe what it sells.
segments.tr: اسأل معظم الناس عمّا تفعله الشركة، وسيصفون لك ما تبيعه.

segments.src: But look at the income statement of almost any manufacturer, retailer, or restaurant group and you'll find the same thing: the biggest number isn't payroll or rent.
segments.tr: لكن انظر إلى قائمة الدخل لأي شركة تصنيع أو تجزئة أو مجموعة مطاعم تقريباً، وستجد الأمر نفسه: الرقم الأكبر ليس الرواتب ولا الإيجار.

segments.src: It's what the company **bought** — raw materials, components, packaging, freight, contract services.
segments.tr: بل ما **اشترته** الشركة، أي المواد الخام والمكونات والتغليف والشحن والخدمات التعاقدية.

segments.src: In many manufacturing firms, purchased goods and services eat more than half of every sales dollar.
segments.tr: في كثير من شركات التصنيع، تستهلك السلع والخدمات المشتراة أكثر من نصف كل دولار من المبيعات.

segments.src: That's why procurement matters, and why it's the sixth stop in this series.
segments.tr: ولهذا تكتسب المشتريات أهميتها، ولهذا تأتي في هذه السلسلة بوصفها المحطة السادسة.

segments.src: Here are the four ideas that hold it together.
segments.tr: إليك الأفكار الأربع التي تُشكّل جوهرها.

segments.src: Purchasing is a transaction.
segments.tr: الشراء معاملة.

segments.src: Procurement is a strategy.**
segments.tr: أما المشتريات فهي استراتيجية.**

segments.src: Purchasing is the narrow act of issuing a purchase order and paying the invoice.
segments.tr: الشراء هو الفعل المحدود المتمثل في إصدار أمر شراء ودفع الفاتورة.

segments.src: Procurement is the whole arc around it: figuring out what the business actually needs, deciding whether to make it in-house or buy it, finding and qualifying suppliers, negotiating terms, and managing performance for years afterward.
segments.tr: أما إدارة المشتريات فهي المنظومة الكاملة حوله: تحديد ما تحتاجه الشركة فعلاً، والقرار بين التصنيع الداخلي أو الشراء الخارجي، والبحث عن الموردين وتأهيلهم، والتفاوض على الشروط، وإدارة الأداء على مدى سنوات لاحقة.

segments.src: Purchasing asks "what's the price?"
segments.tr: الشراء يسأل: «ما السعر؟»

segments.src: Procurement asks "what's the **total cost of ownership**?"
segments.tr: أما المشتريات فتسأل: «ما **إجمالي تكلفة الملكية**؟»
